Repair and extend the H3Act offline evidence pipeline in `/workspace/project`.
Its typed payload models, frame adapter and client replay must work together
with compressed byte expressions and the origin-capture audit extension.
Produce exact client receipts, lifecycle outcomes, HTTP/1.1 request boundaries,
body summaries, source-byte attribution and paired evidence diagnostics.
The complete input/output and timing contract is `/workspace/PROTOCOL.md`.
Runtime, dependency, submission-tree and syscall limits are in `RUNTIME.md`.
The initial project has real integration defects and unfinished extension modules.
Keep useful behavior while implementing the complete documented domain.
You may reorganize the project or add source/data files within the tree budget.
Submit the whole `/workspace/project` tree; its CLI entry is `main.py`.
Use CPython3.11.14 and the provisioned Pydantic2.12.5 dependency set.
Run `cd /workspace/project && python3 -B main.py < /workspace/sample.json`.
Run `python3 /workspace/check.py /workspace/project` for public sanity checks.
The program reads one UTF-8 JSON object and writes one JSON object, without args.
Public checks cover only small examples; all published domain rules apply.


Work in /workspace. When finished run exactly: echo COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT
items.finalText:
The implementation is complete and verified. Final summary of the work:

## Repairs to existing integration defects
- **`modules/fuzz_adapter.py`** — fixed the `NameError`/broken frame conversion; the receipt encoder now emits the exact documented encoding (8-byte time, 4-byte stream, kind byte, pair/data content, end byte), with datagram end bytes forced to 0 and send errors raised after request end.
- **`HTTP3_Just_Send.py`** — fixed the late-response-waiter defect (a response end retained while still sending now yields `ok` at send-finish), timeouts that leaked past termination, closes that ignored paused senders, and events accepted after termination/response end.
- **`modules/clock.py`** — correct equal-time priority order (case starts → external events → pause completions → timeouts), zero-pause yielding, deterministic heap ordering.
- **`main.py`** — full strict input validation: duplicate keys, nonfinite/overflowing numbers, BOM, invalid UTF‑8/lone surrogates, exact key sets, frame field rules and defaults, name/seed charsets, every documented budget and 2⁶³−1 range.

## Completed extension modules
- **`modules/byte_program.py`** — rope algebra (leaf/concat/repeat) with cached exact fingerprints, doubling-based repeat hashes, iterative slicing/range-hash/materialize (multi-GB sequences never expand), the full byte-expression grammar validated through CPython's `ast` (depth ≤128, literals/names/`+`/`*`/slices), and template compilation with `{{...}}` expressions and `<<random_string>>` = SHA256(`seed/coordinate/occurrence`)[:20].
- **`modules/capture_audit.py`** — complete HTTP/1.1 framing: CRLF line rules with the 8193-byte prefix rule, request/header grammar, 65536-byte/128-field blocks, Content-Length list rules, single `chunked` Transfer-Encoding, opaque length bodies, chunked bodies (hex size/suffix/CRLF/trailers with forbidden names), streaming field-block fingerprints, per-part `committed`, `owner`/`owners` attribution, all request and paired case flags, and the 20000-request/40000-chunk-line budgets.

## Verification
- Public checker: **PASS** (3 fixtures), sample output byte-identical to the published expectation.
- ~700 targeted assertions (validation, HTTP edges, expressions/templates, lifecycle, flags, frame defaults, provenance) all green.
- ~2500 randomized trials cross-validated against two independently written references (direct lifecycle simulator + byte-level HTTP parser), including expression/random-token templates — this found and resolved real defects (rope slice ordering, memory blow-up, `owners` merging semantics).
- Worst in-domain loads: ≤14 s CPU, ≤85 MB RSS (scored limits 20 s / 512 MiB); submission tree is 10 regular files (~64 KB) with `main.py` as CLI entry.
